q: By March 31, 2027, the United States actually imposes tariffs under the U.S. Russia sanctions law (the Graham Act) on at least one country (the tariffs must be in effect and not waived)
basis: On October 16, two days before the law's tariffs were due to take effect, the president waived the tariffs and most of the sanctions indefinitely, and the Abu Dhabi talks on November 10–11 agreed in principle on a prisoner exchange but ended without progress on territory. Two developments could prompt withdrawal of the waiver: the end in mid-December of the impact review of up to 60 days announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and pressure from Congress, where Democrats take the majority in January. If the tariffs were applied to China, however, they would collide with the U.S.-China tariff truce, which runs until January 10, 2027. There is a precedent: in August 2025 Washington actually imposed tariffs on India. This forecast tests whether the pressure side of the top-ranked U.S. course is carried out.
rs: White House proclamations and executive orders, and the Federal Register
